subject: phoenix
pitch:
Category: Fantastical creature.
Subject: phoenix with flame plumage, wings spread.
Style: Genshin Impact.
reasoning:
I'm figuring out the most impactful, minimal edits that will exact-match cleanly. Looking at the renders, the wings seem off—the feathers look too thin and sparse, spreading from the arm edge-on so they appear as flat bars from the front, which suggests the feather plane orientation needs rethinking.

The body also feels too small relative to the wings, and the head is tiny compared to the Genshin-style proportions I'm aiming for, so I'm considering bumping up skull scale and enlarging the eye decals to make the face read better. The tail ribbons look fine but a bit sparse, and the floating embers just need a visual pass for density.

The pillar placement checks out — feet land right at the pillar top near y=0.52 with no floating issue. But the chest area is too covered in gold leaf decoration, burying the head visually, so I want to enlarge the skull and beak (bumping beak radius from 0.036 to roughly 0.045) to give the head more presence against the collar clutter.

I'm also considering adding a glowing sun-disc halo ring behind the bird, maybe around y=1.3 and z=-0.6, to frame the head from the front — though I need to check whether the tail plumes would awkwardly pass through it.

Rather than the halo ring, I'll scatter small glowing flame cards along the top of the wing arm tubes where the surface normal points upward, giving the wings a licking-flame plumage effect without heavy occlusion.

Checking other details now: the feather extrusion asymmetry and ground-sink are fine as-is, and the drooping gold crest ribbons read well. I want to tweak eye placement and size on the skull decal, making it slightly bigger and shifted, and I'm considering adding a subtle glow to the eye decal texture to make it read as luminous.

Now I'm listing the concrete edits to make: bump up the skull scale, enlarge the beak and jaw radii, adjust the eye decal block with new position and size, nudge brow positions slightly outward to match the bigger skull, and double-check the forehead hit point still lands correctly. I'm matching the exact search strings for the skull scale line and the six-line eye decal block so I can replace them precisely, then adding flame cards scattered along the arm after the existing tuft cards line, using arm surface scatter with a distance filter.
